title: Sell Mineral Rights in Basin, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Basin, WY | Big Horn County Seat
metaDescription: Basin, WY is the Big Horn County seat and the courthouse of record for the county's legacy oil fields. Get a plain read on your mineral interest before you sell.
heroLead: Basin is the Big Horn County seat, which means the courthouse here holds the actual paper trail for every mineral interest I work with in this county, going back to the earliest oil leases in the basin.
intro: The Bighorn Basin's oil fields, Elk Basin, Byron, Grass Creek, Oregon Basin, are some of the oldest producing ground in Wyoming, with leasing and drilling records stretching back to the 1910s and 20s. Because Basin sits at the county's administrative center, every deed, lease, and probate order tied to those fields eventually runs through the Big Horn County recorder's office right here in town.
If you inherited a mineral interest anywhere in this county, there's a good chance the paperwork that proves your ownership was filed within a few blocks of where I'd be pulling it.

sections.heading: Legacy fields, legacy paperwork
paragraphs: A hundred years of ownership changes means the chain of title on a lot of Big Horn County minerals runs through multiple probate proceedings, name changes, and old-style legal descriptions that don't always match how land gets described today. Untangling that chain is most of the work before I can quote anything honestly.
The upside of a county this well-documented is that once title is confirmed, it tends to hold up cleanly, because so many transactions have already run through the same recorder's office.

sections.heading: What determines value countywide
paragraphs: Most of Big Horn County's production today comes from mature, secondary-recovery fields with gentler decline curves than newer shale plays, but also less upside. I price a Basin-area interest against actual royalty statements when there's a production history, or against comparable undeveloped-acreage trades when there isn't.

Being the courthouse town itself doesn't change the geology under Basin specifically, but it does mean I can often confirm a chain of title faster here than in counties where records are scattered across multiple offices or have been transferred between jurisdictions over the years.

faqs.question: Why does everything route through Basin?
faqs.answer: Basin is the county seat, so the Big Horn County recorder's office here holds the official records for the whole county, regardless of which town your specific tract sits near.

faqs.question: My deed has an old-style legal description. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not usually. I can match older section-based descriptions to current plats without much trouble.

faqs.question: Are Big Horn County fields still producing?
faqs.answer: Several are, under secondary and enhanced recovery. I'll check your specific tract's current status.

faqs.question: How long does title confirmation take in Big Horn County?
faqs.answer: Usually just a few days, since the records are centralized here in Basin and generally well organized.
